The Hypocrisy of Ed Miliband and the UK Labour Government’s Israel Policy-- A long read if interested in a thorough rebuttal of his speech.  The Hypocrisy of Ed Miliband and the UK Labour Government’s Israel Policy A line-by-line deconstruction of the “You Were Right” speech On 28 September, in Liverpool, the Foreign Secretary of the United Kingdom stood in front of a hall of people who have spent two years marching under “from the river to the sea” and told them they were right. The speech deserves an answer, line by line. “As we think about our role in the world, we will never be silent about injustice and suffering.” Never silent. Let us test that. In June 2025 this government endorsed Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara — a territory under military occupation since 1975, settled by the occupying power, whose native population has sat in refugee camps in Algeria for fifty years. Britain does not ban goods from occupied Western Sahara. It grants them preferential access under its trade agreement with Morocco. Turkey has occupied northern Cyprus since 1974, moved in settlers and partitioned an EU member state; Britain is a guarantor power there and sells Turkey weapons. Then there is Tibet, Xinjiang, the prisons of Iran, and Sudan, where mass killing has proceeded for three years in near-total silence from this podium. Silence is not the word for British foreign policy. Selectivity is. Of every occupation on the planet, exactly one draws an import ban, a supply-chain interdiction and a bespoke sanctions regime, and it is the Jewish one. “The only route to peace is two states, a secure Israel and a secure Palestine, with freedom, dignity, and self-determination for both peoples.” Like the two states of Gaza and Israel. In 2005 Israel removed every soldier, every settlement and every grave from Gaza. That is what a withdrawal looks like when a country actually means it. Within two years Hamas held the territory; within eighteen it produced the 7th of October. The formula is recited in London as though it has never been attempted. It was attempted, unilaterally, at enormous domestic cost, and the answer came back first in rockets and then in a massacre. A serious foreign secretary would spend his conference speech asking what happened between the withdrawal and the massacre. Mr Miliband simply repeats the formula in a firmer voice and calls it a reset. “Hamas's murderous attack on October the 7th united the vast majority of the world in rightful condemnation.” Not really, and only for about a fortnight. The dead had not all been identified before the marches began, and they were not marches against Hamas. The condemnation was real and it was brief, and its expiry date is the single most revealing fact of the last three years. Note who Mr Miliband has chosen to address in this speech: not the people whose condemnation held, but the people whose condemnation lapsed first. “We stand, I say, against antisemitism wherever we find it and in whatever form.” The Equality and Human Rights Commission found that his party broke the Equality Act — unlawful harassment and discrimination against Jews. That is a finding in law, not a matter of opinion, and it was made about his own party, five years after he led it. Since October 2023 antisemitic incidents in Britain have run at record levels: Jewish schoolchildren advised to cover their uniforms on public transport, synagogues under guard, students hounded off campuses. And it is to the movement that supplied a good deal of that atmosphere that the Foreign Secretary says: you were right. Wherever we find it — except here, except now, except in this room. “This party will always recognise the threats Israel faces and stand emphatically against those who seek its destruction.” This is the same government that suspended arms export licences to Israel and has now widened the policy to refuse anything judged to contribute to the occupation, indefinitely. You cannot stand emphatically against a country's destruction while rationing what it is permitted to defend itself with against the people attempting that destruction. Nor can you stand against them while telling their loudest supporters in Britain, from the stage of your own conference, that their judgement was sound. “But this cannot justify the suffering the Netanyahu government has inflicted in Gaza and the West Bank. This suffering is a stain on the conscience of the world.” Read the construction carefully, because the argument is in the grammar. The suffering was “inflicted by the Netanyahu government” — not caused by a war, and certainly not by the side that began it, refused every ceasefire that required it to give up the hostages and its weapons, and then fought from beneath hospitals, schools and apartment blocks. Hamas could have ended the war on any day of it, and chose instead to go on fighting at the expense of its own civilian population. But for Mr Miliband, everything is Israel's fault, and the sentence is built so that nothing else can be said. And as for the stain on the conscience of the world. Britain did not kill German civilians incidentally. It set out to. The Area Bombing Directive of 14 February 1942 instructed Bomber Command “to focus attacks on the morale of the enemy civil population and in particular the industrial workers.” The following day the Chief of the Air Staff removed any remaining ambiguity: “the aiming points will be the built up areas, and not, for instance, the dockyards or aircraft factories.” Civilians were not collateral damage in the British campaign. They were the target, by written order, signed and filed. The bill came to something on the order of four hundred thousand German civilians. Forty thousand in Hamburg in a single week. Dresden. The cities of the Ruhr. No telephone calls to the occupants, no leaflet naming the building, no evacuation map by grid square. And the Allies killed at least sixty-eight thousand French civilians, more than fifty thousand of them in Normandy alone, in the course of liberating France — more Frenchmen killed by British and American bombs than Britons killed by German ones in the whole of the Blitz. Was the liberation of Europe a stain on the conscience of the world? Or was it a war against an enemy that had to be beaten and that fought from among its own people? Britain does not apply to its own history the standard it has just written into law for somebody else's present. If it did, no British government since Churchill's would survive the audit. “To the millions of people in this country and indeed elsewhere, who have been moved and outraged by the plight of the Palestinian people: we hear you. You were right.” Right about what? This is the sentence that ought to follow Mr Miliband for the rest of his career, because he does not say. Right that Israel is committing genocide? Right that it should never have been founded? Right to chant for a Palestine from the river to the sea? That slogan is not a demand for a state alongside Israel. It names the whole of the land, from the Jordan to the Mediterranean, and what stands on most of that land today is Israel. It is a demand for the destruction of the Jewish state, and it leaves no room for the seven million Jews living between those two points. Everybody chanting it understands this perfectly well, and so does the Foreign Secretary. The movement he is congratulating has nothing whatever to say about a regime that throws gay men from rooftops, denies women equal standing in law, conscripts children and executes its critics in the street. It went quiet about the hostages within a week. Its outrage has always had a very specific shape, and the Foreign Secretary has just validated it without once specifying what he is validating. Here is what a serious government would say instead: that Palestinians are adults and political actors, responsible for what they do. That their leadership tried to annihilate the Jews of Palestine before there was a State of Israel to object to. That they refused partition in 1947 and invaded; refused negotiation at Khartoum in 1967; refused Barak and Clinton in 2000 and answered with the bombing of the buses and the cafés; refused Olmert in 2008 without so much as a reply. A century of no, and not one British minister has ever suggested that the people saying it might bear some responsibility for where it has left them. “We call out ethnic cleansing by the settler terrorists in the West Bank.” Words have meanings, and this one has a meaning. Settler violence is real, it is criminal, and Israel should prosecute far more of it than it does — that is a fair criticism and Israelis make it loudly in their own press and their own courts. It is not ethnic cleansing. The Palestinian population of the West Bank has grown from roughly six hundred thousand in 1967 to more than three million today. Populations being cleansed do not multiply fivefold. The Foreign Secretary reached for the gravest charge in the vocabulary of atrocity and attached it to a phenomenon whose defining feature — the removal of a people — has demonstrably not occurred. Ethnic cleansing did occur in this conflict. It occurred in 1948, in the Jewish Quarter of Jerusalem, emptied of every last Jew by the Jordanian army. It occurred across the Arab world, where some 850,000 Jews were stripped, expelled or driven out of communities two and a half thousand years old, from Baghdad to Tripoli to Sana'a. Britain has never once called that out. There is no import ban attached to it, no sanctions regime, no reset. And note what is now offered as the remedy. The settlement Britain has recognised and intends to enforce would make eastern Jerusalem the capital of a Palestinian state. Consider what that means. Eastern Jerusalem is Arab today for precisely one reason: in 1948 the Jordanian army expelled every Jew living there, dynamited their synagogues and barred their return for nineteen years. Jews had been the largest community in Jerusalem since the nineteenth century. The proposal on the table is to take the one piece of ground in this entire conflict that was successfully and completely cleansed of its Jews, and award it in perpetuity to the side that did the cleansing. Britain's stated objection to Israeli settlements is that territory may not be acquired by force. Run that principle across eastern Jerusalem and it comes out the other way: Jordan took it by force in a war of aggression, held it illegally for nineteen years, and lost it in a war it chose to join. The principle is only ever made to run in one direction. This is not the correction of an injustice. It is the ratification of one — a rule that ethnic cleansing confers good title, provided the people cleansed were Jews. “We call out the evidence of war crimes in Gaza.” Whose evidence? The casualty figures that drive every one of these findings come from a health ministry run by Hamas, do not distinguish combatants from civilians, and are then recirculated by institutions with their own record — including an aid agency several of whose employees are alleged to have taken part in the attacks of 7 October, and many more to have cheered them on. Serious allegations deserve serious investigation, and Israel's own courts have a longer record of prosecuting Israeli soldiers than most of Israel's critics have of prosecuting anyone at all. What Mr Miliband has is a conclusion in search of a citation. Set against that, consider the people who study this for a living. John Spencer, chair of urban warfare studies at the Modern War Institute at West Point, has said that Israel implemented more measures to prevent civilian casualties than any military in history, and warned that it has set a standard that will be hard, and perhaps impossible, for any Western army to repeat. Colonel Richard Kemp — a British officer, former commander of British forces in Afghanistan — has said the same of successive Gaza campaigns. These are not publicists. They are the professionals whose job is to know what urban warfare costs. Nor are they alone, and this is the part Mr Miliband should find hardest to dismiss. The High Level Military Group — eleven former chiefs of staff, generals and senior defence officials from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Australia and Colombia, chaired by General Klaus Naumann, former Chief of Staff of the Bundeswehr and Chairman of NATO's Military Committee — went to Israel, examined the conduct of the Gaza campaign, and reported that Israel “not only met a reasonable international standard of observance of the laws of armed conflict, but in many cases significantly exceeded that standard.” They added that none of them was aware of any army that had taken such extensive measures to protect an enemy civilian population, and that Israel's adherence to the laws of war had cost Israeli soldiers and Israeli civilians their lives. They delivered that assessment to the United Nations Human Rights Council's own Commission of Inquiry, which proceeded as though it had never been written. In August 2024 the same body returned to the subject, submitting to the International Criminal Court that the Prosecutor's allegation of a deliberate policy of starvation was “unsupported by all available evidence,” that Gaza is the most complex and challenging battlefield of modern times, and — this is the sentence for the Foreign Secretary — that the standard being applied to Israel is an unbearable and unrealistic one that no democratic army conducting similar operations could meet. That includes the British Army. Mr Miliband is legislating against Israel on a basis that would convict his own soldiers, and NATO's most senior retired officers have told him so in writing. Since October 7th the judgement has been tested again, by people who went and looked. General Sir John McColl — former Deputy Supreme Allied Commander Europe, which is to say one of the most senior officers Britain has produced in a generation — led a team of military experts from six NATO countries into Israel and observed operations in Rafah. His conclusion, published in The Times: “I came away from the trip satisfied that the IDF's operations and rules of engagement were rigorous compared to the British Army and our Western allies.” He recorded operations aborted because of the danger to civilians, and tunnels running beneath schools, hospitals and mosques. Britain's own former deputy commander of NATO forces in Europe has compared the Israeli army's rules of engagement to Britain's, and found Israel's the stricter of the two. A parallel American assessment reached the same place. A task force of seven retired US flag officers — among them General David Rodriguez, former commander of AFRICOM, Admiral Michael Rogers, former head of US Cyber Command, and General Charles Wald, former deputy commander of EUCOM — concluded that the IDF had prosecuted the campaign “with operational and tactical excellence and in overall compliance with the Law of Armed Conflict,” and that the United States military would benefit from studying how Israel fought in so complex an environment. That same group criticised Israel sharply on other grounds, which is rather the point: these are not advocates. They are professionals who found fault where they found it, and did not find it here. And consider what the measures actually are, because no army has ever done anything like them. Leaflets naming the buildings to be struck. Telephone calls and Arabic-language text messages to the occupants of specific apartments. Evacuation maps published by numbered grid block. Roof-knocking. Daily humanitarian pauses and corridors held open while the enemy used them to move. Every one of those warnings also warns Hamas, which is the point most often missed: Israel has repeatedly traded away operational surprise, and with it the lives of its own soldiers, to reduce the deaths of the civilians of a population that elected its enemy. Britain did not telephone Hamburg. The United States did not publish grid maps of Fallujah. No one has ever fought this way, and the reward for it has been a British import ban. “We call out Israel's illegal occupation of Palestine.” Occupation of what, taken from whom? Between 1948 and 1967 Judea and Samaria were held by Jordan and Gaza by Egypt — seized in a war of aggression and recognised by almost no one on earth. Jordan expelled every Jew from the Jewish Quarter, destroyed or desecrated some fifty-eight synagogues, used the headstones of the Mount of Olives for paving and latrines, and barred Jews from the Western Wall for nineteen years in open breach of the armistice it had signed. Britain, which had governed the place until the day before, said almost nothing. Jordan then stripped its Palestinians of citizenship in 1988 and walked away from them. There was no Palestinian state there to occupy, for the simple reason that the Arab leadership had refused one in 1947. “We will ban the import of goods from illegal settlements. We will disrupt the supply lines of British finance, British construction, and British services for illegal settlements.” Then ban the others. Britain has never in its history banned imports from an occupied territory — not from Western Sahara, whose produce it actively privileges; not from northern Cyprus, held by Turkey for fifty-two years with settlers moved in, while Britain maintains a free trade agreement with Ankara and sells it weapons. Britain does not ban goods from Xinjiang, where a million people have been put through camps and forced labour is systematic. Yet Britain goes on importing tens of billions of pounds a year from China. “When it comes to the attempt to destroy the two-state solution, this party, this movement, this government says: we will not let you succeed.” Britain recognised a Palestinian state in 2025 — with no agreed border, no demilitarisation, no functioning government, no recognition of Israel required in return, and with hostages still held in tunnels. Whatever else that achieved, it established a principle and taught a lesson. The lesson is that you may refuse every offer put to you for a hundred years, launch the largest massacre of Jews since the Holocaust, hold the bodies of the murdered as bargaining chips, and be handed statehood anyway, having conceded nothing at all. That is not a two-state policy. It is a policy that rewards rejectionism. If anyone is destroying the two-state solution it is Britain and the European governments that have decided appeasing a movement founded on the destruction of the Jewish homeland is the way to resolve a dispute about whether that homeland may exist. Mr Miliband says he will not let anyone destroy the two-state solution, but his government's policies encourage the maximalist goals of a movement that refuses to accept the legitimacy and the rights of the Jewish state. That is not a condition that leads to a peaceful resolution of anything. The Defining Principle So we are left with a government that bans settlement wine and not Xinjiang cotton. But look harder at the inconsistency, because it is sharper than it first appears. Northern Cyprus has been under Turkish occupation since 1974 — the territory of a sovereign state, seized by force from a government that still exists and still claims it, with settlers imported to change the demography. Western Sahara has been under Moroccan occupation since 1975, and Britain does not merely tolerate that one: it endorses Morocco's plan for the territory and grants its produce preferential access to the British market. Two unambiguous occupations, one of them against a member of the European Union, and from Britain not a ban, not a sanction, not a word. Then there is the occupation Britain has chosen to act upon, which is the only one nobody can define. Occupied from whom? There has never been a Palestinian state in Judea and Samaria. The territory was held illegally by Jordan for nineteen years, before that by Britain itself, and before that by the Ottomans. There is no dispossessed sovereign waiting to have it restored. The Foreign Office is sanctioning an occupation whose victim it cannot name, while ignoring two whose victims it could name in a sentence. And underneath the inconsistency sits something worse than inconsistency. To call the Jewish presence in Judea and Samaria an occupation is to declare that Jews are foreigners on the one piece of ground on earth that is named after them. Britain is not neutral on that question any longer; it has taken a side. It has decided that Hebron and Shiloh are places where Jews do not belong, and that the Palestinian state it proposes to midwife must be emptied of them before it can be born. A government that would treat the demand to clear any other territory of any other people as a scandal has adopted it here as policy. So the stated principle — we will never be silent about injustice — plainly is not the operative one. Something else is selecting the targets, and it is not hard to find. The Labour Party has discovered that Gaza is a direct threat to Labour's hold on power. In July 2024 five pro-Gaza independents took seats from Labour, there were double-digit swings against the party across constituencies with large Muslim populations, and the present Health Secretary held his own seat by a few hundred votes against an independent running on a single issue. In May 2026 Labour lost close to fifteen hundred council seats, with its Muslim vote fragmenting to the Greens, to independents and to the new party on its left. In July Sir Keir Starmer was gone. In September the Foreign Secretary stood up at conference and announced a reset. Read those four dates in order and the foreign policy explains itself. This is not a moral position arrived at through reflection on injustice. It is a price list. Sanctioning China would cost Britain tens of billions and its supply chains. Sanctioning Turkey would cost it a NATO partner and a trade deal. Confronting Morocco would cost it influence in North Africa. Sanctioning Israel costs Britain a rounding error in trade and buys back a bloc of marginal seats and, with them, a grip on power. Of every injustice on the Foreign Secretary's list, the Jewish state is simply the cheapest item on the shelf. Mr Miliband said: we hear you. He does, and that is precisely the objection. He heard a constituency, not an argument. The Test His Own Party Wrote There is an objection that will be raised against everything written here, which is that Ed Miliband is Jewish and the grandson of refugees, and is therefore beyond this particular reproach. He is not. Being Jewish confers no immunity from applying a double standard, and no special insight into one either. Jews hold every political opinion available to human beings, including those that assure the world its suspicions about the Jewish state were correct all along. A policy is judged by the policy, not by the ancestry of the minister announcing it. And there is a test. It has a definition, and his own party adopted it. In September 2018 the Labour Party formally accepted the IHRA working definition of antisemitism together with all of its illustrative examples, one of which is applying double standards to Israel “by requiring of it a behavior not expected or demanded of any other democratic nation.” Now read back over what this government has done. It has never in its history banned imports from an occupied territory, and has now banned them from one. It privileges the produce of occupied Western Sahara and interdicts the produce of Judea and Samaria. It rations arms to a democracy fighting for its survival while trading freely with Turkey and China. It holds the Israeli army to a standard that NATO's own former commanders have said in writing no Western army could meet. That is not antisemitism by implication or inference. It is the example, almost word for word, as the Labour Party itself wrote it down and signed it. Mr Miliband is not calling for Jews to be harmed, and nothing here suggests that he wants it. But policy does not run on intentions. He has told a movement that marches under a slogan with no room in it for the seven million Jews living between the river and the sea that its judgement was sound, and he has lent it the authority of the Foreign Office to say so. Whatever he believes privately, the people who do want Jews harmed left Mr Miliband's speech stronger, better funded and more confident than they arrived. They, unlike him, know exactly what they mean. The Foreign Secretary told that hall he was guided by survivor's responsibility. His family survived because somewhere a state's door was open and a war was fought to the end against an enemy that hid behind civilians. He might reflect on which side of that inheritance he was speaking for on Monday.

WHO'S COMING FOR US NEXT (3/3) Chapter 3 of 6: RUSSIA — The Wounded Bear With the Bomb Section C of 3: NATO's Edge, Russia's Partners, and the Restraints Project WCFUN — Status FF — October 2, 2026 Kaliningrad is a launch platform and a hostage. The Suwałki Gap is a planner's problem, not evidence of a thrust this month. The restraint that matters is whether the war is still consuming the army. Posts 1 and 2 covered the arsenal, the doctrine, the ladder, the cost of the war, and the rebuilding. This post covers where NATO and Russia physically meet, Russia's partners, and what restrains Moscow. Terms: NATO and Article 5 are defined in Post 1. The Suwałki Gap is the Polish-Lithuanian border strip between Kaliningrad and Belarus, the only land link between the Baltic states and the rest of NATO. GRU is Russian military intelligence and FSB the domestic security service. A "wiper" is malware built to destroy data, not steal it. KALININGRAD AND THE SUWAŁKI GAP Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave on the Baltic, bordered by Poland and Lithuania, housing the Baltic Fleet and nuclear-capable Iskander missiles. The Gap is commonly described as about 65 kilometers wide at its narrowest, sometimes nearer 100, depending on where the line is drawn. On September 30, 2026, NATO spokesperson Allison Hart confirmed a written Russian message; Post 1 covers its nuclear warning. Western officers have said key installations in Kaliningrad would be a likely first target if Russia attacked a NATO ally. Lithuania called the new threats psychological pressure. Poland's foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, argued for more exercises near the exclave. One summary of the Reuters reporting says a Russian Mi-8 helicopter crossed from Kaliningrad into Poland near Braniewo on September 23. That is single-source and unconfirmed. A Western military source told Reuters that dozens of NATO aircraft ran an unannounced operation around Kaliningrad in mid-August 2026 to show they could disrupt its radar and air-defense links. Much of the exclave's ground force was drawn down for Ukraine. In a crisis Kaliningrad is a launch platform and a hostage to reinforcement. Disrupting the Gap would not need a large invasion to complicate reinforcing three NATO members at once. No evidence in this chapter shows Russia preparing to seize it now. A drone incident, an infrastructure attack, or a perceived blockade matters more than a scripted thrust. NATO'S EASTERN EDGE NATO has nine multinational Forward Land Forces battlegroups from Finland to Bulgaria, and a German-led brigade in Lithuania is moving toward full operational capability. Eastern Sentry, an ongoing mission along the eastern border, answered Russian aircraft and drone violations after Baltic Sentry in January 2025. In September 2025 about two dozen Russian drones entered Polish airspace; Warsaw halted flights at four airports, and only two drones were intercepted. One analyst quoted by Al Jazeera said European air defenses are "outdated by at least five years." The flank is stronger than in 2021 and still thin against a fully rebuilt Russian force. Battlegroups are tripwires, not corps-sized defenses. Eastern Sentry shows the alliance can answer air incursions quickly. It does not prove NATO can sustain a ground fight without American enablers. HYBRID WARFARE: SABOTAGE, CABLES, AND DRONES In November 2025 an explosion damaged a Polish railway used for aid to Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it sabotage and said two Ukrainian suspects were believed hired by Russia. The Kremlin denied it. The 2026 ATA cites it as disruption of Ukraine's support networks. Polish officials said a Colombian man arrested for fires at construction depots was recruited over Telegram and told to film them for Russian state television. Finnish police detained the cargo ship Fitburg on December 31, 2025, on suspicion of damaging a Helsinki–Tallinn cable. Police said its anchor dragged the seabed for tens of kilometers. This is an investigation, not a conviction. One outlet reports that in August 2026 a quadcopter carrying plastic explosives struck a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig/Halle, a NATO airlift hub, and failed to detonate. That account is unconfirmed. Al Jazeera says U.S. intelligence reportedly assessed the drone as Russian-made, and Russia dismissed such claims as scare stories. Drone sightings canceled hundreds of flights at German airports in autumn 2025, and attribution there is less settled than for the rail sabotage. Not every drone over a NATO border is Russian. Ukrainian drones aimed at Russian Baltic oil terminals have strayed into Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, and Finland since March 23, 2026. On April 10, 2026, the Baltic foreign ministers rejected Russian claims that they let Ukraine use their airspace. Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo assessed that Russian jamming likely drove the drones off course. These are probes. Each tests what NATO notices, names, and does. A drone over a base is one fact. Who sent it is a separate fact that needs its own evidence. Most of these acts have drawn statements, sanctions, and investigations, which teaches Moscow that many stay cheap relative to open war. CYBER, ELECTIONS, AND SPACE In December 2025 a wiper called DynoWiper was used against Poland's power grid. It did not cause a blackout. On July 13, 2026, the United Kingdom and the European Union attributed it to the FSB's Centre 16. The Register reports it could have left half a million people without power in winter. Early technical analysis had linked the malware to Sandworm, a GRU-associated group, so the official attribution names a different agency. The disagreement shows how hard attribution is. It does not change the conclusion that Russian state hackers tried to cut power to a NATO member in winter. The 2026 ATA calls Russia a persistent cyber and foreign-intelligence threat that uses attacks, disinformation, influence operations, and energy-market manipulation, and often denies its role. In September 2024 the Justice Department seized 32 domains used in a campaign called Doppelganger, some imitating outlets such as the Washington Post and Fox News, and indicted two RT employees over a $10 million operation aimed partly at U.S. voters. That is a court record. Reporting this month names Storm-1516, Storm-1679, and Matryoshka as active against the 2026 midterms, and says the FBI's Foreign Influence Task Force and two related offices have been shut down. That account is secondhand, from commentator David Corn of a left-leaning outlet, and the reasons for any closures are not established here. Russia has tried to influence American voters across administrations. Agencies that countered it have also been criticized from both parties for overreach. The best defense is a public that checks a story before it shares it. The 2026 ATA says Russia is developing a satellite meant to carry a nuclear weapon as an antisatellite system. A nuclear burst in orbit would indiscriminately damage navigation, communications, missile-warning, and commercial services, including Russian and Chinese satellites. Its value is coercive threat more than a clean military option. THE ARCTIC NATO launched Arctic Sentry on February 11, 2026, under Joint Force Command Norfolk. It creates no new standing force. NATO says Russia has set up a new Arctic command, reopened Soviet-era sites, and is testing novel weapons. In June 2026 NATO activated Forward Land Forces Finland, led by Sweden. Cold Response 2026 put about 25,000 troops from 14 nations into Norway and Finland in March. Russia deployed all eight of its nuclear icebreakers at once in December 2025, a first, to keep export routes open. Three more of the new class are under construction. The Leader-class Rossiya, meant for year-round transit around 2030, has slipped repeatedly. The United States operates two aging heavy icebreakers and signed a $6.1 billion deal with Finland in October 2025 for 11 new vessels, first delivery expected in 2028. The Northern Fleet and the Kola Peninsula hold the core of Russia's sea-based nuclear force. Finnish and Swedish membership put NATO on the Nordic land mass facing Kola. Russia's answer is the one it uses elsewhere: rebuild the ground force stripped for Ukraine, leave the nuclear fleet untouched, and treat icebreakers as strategic infrastructure. The Bear Gap near Svalbard is the naval cousin of the Suwałki problem, because Russia need not invade Norway to threaten reinforcement of the northern flank. CHINA, IRAN, AND NORTH KOREA The 2026 ATA says China's imports of Russian oil and gas are key revenue for Moscow, and that North Korean and Iranian military support have helped Russia in Ukraine. North Korea sent about 14,000 to 15,000 soldiers to Kursk in 2024; Defense News reports about 9,500 remained as of mid-2026. Sources cited by CRS and Defense News put North Korean deliveries at about 4 million artillery shells since mid-2023 and 148 KN-23 and KN-24 missiles by early 2025, with 40 more by mid-2026. Ukrainian officials estimate North Korea supplies about half of Russia's frontline munitions, an interested party's estimate. Iran supplied Shahed drones and the knowledge to build them. Chapter 4 covers North Korea. Reporting on the 2026 Middle East war lists Russian help to Iran, including satellite imagery, target lists, drone components, and man-portable air-defense systems. Claims of fighter jets and thousands of missiles appear in fewer sources and are unconfirmed. Intelligence sharing is better supported than the largest hardware claims. The relationship is transactional. Each government takes what it needs. None has promised to fight for the others. They supply each other's weak points while the United States faces all of them at once. That is not an alliance. It is a set of overlapping workshops. BEYOND EUROPE Russia's Africa Corps, the Defense Ministry unit that replaced Wagner in Mali, has about 2,000 to 2,500 troops there by most estimates. After offensives that began April 25, 2026, Foreign Policy reports it was forced to retreat from Kidal, and also says it helped thwart a jihadist offensive on Bamako. Human Rights Watch documented airstrikes on June 15, 2026, that killed eight civilians, and a July 10 raid in which its fighters killed nine. Africa shows Russia exporting regime protection cheaply, and the limits of that model. The 2026 ATA says Russia probably wants to expand ties with Cuba, Nicaragua, and Venezuela. A September 2026 RAND assessment found the Ukraine war has not stopped pursuit of objectives in Cuba, Venezuela, Nicaragua, and Brazil, and noted Russia cannot threaten the U.S. homeland conventionally from the hemisphere. These are places to impose costs and force Washington to spend attention, not invasion routes. NATO'S ACTUAL READINESS At the 2025 Hague summit, members agreed to spend 5 percent of GDP on defense by 2035, with 3.5 percent on core defense and 1.5 percent on related infrastructure. The United States has signaled a reduced day-to-day role in Europe while expecting allies to move faster. IISS finds the Baltic and Nordic regions being integrated into NATO plans, and also finds gaps in personnel, artillery, air defense, ammunition, and sustainment. It judges European forces unlikely to provide the conventional backbone without U.S. resources before 2030. The demand that Europe carry more of its own defense was overdue. A gap between an American reduction and a European buildup is the window Moscow would look for. The shift should be paced to the buildup, not announced ahead of it. Article 5 has never been tested against a Russian move on a Baltic state. No source here assigns a reliable probability or date. WHAT RESTRAINS MOSCOW Four things restrain Russia. The Ukraine war still consumes its army and budget. NATO, including the American nuclear umbrella, is far larger than the force in Ukraine. Beijing benefits from Russia as a partner and has little interest in uncontrolled nuclear brinkmanship. And the record shows Moscow has kept its use of force inside limits it can absorb. None is permanent. The first weakens if the war ends and the army recovers; IISS puts equipment gaps closing by late 2026 or early 2027 and a larger force by the early 2030s. The second depends on allied resolve. The third depends on Beijing. The fourth depends on a small circle of men. A settlement or frozen conflict would free Russian forces and money. What Moscow did with them would depend on what it believed NATO would do. If a settlement arrives, the world will be told the Russian problem is over. That is the moment to be most careful. A Russia that stops bleeding and keeps this production rate is more dangerous within a few years than the Russia of 2021, with a rebuilt army, a war economy, new missiles, a partner in Beijing, and a proven playbook of sabotage. CAPABILITY, INTENT, CONSTRAINT Capability: Russia can destroy American and allied cities with nuclear weapons. It can attack satellites, grids, cables, and elections below the threshold of war. It can threaten the Baltic states and Kaliningrad's surroundings with missiles and, after rebuilding, with ground forces. It cannot invade the United States, and it cannot defeat NATO conventionally if the alliance fights as an alliance. Intent: The record shows intent to subordinate Ukraine, punish states that arm it, erode NATO cohesion, and keep nuclear threats available. It does not show a decision to start a general war with NATO. Constraint: The cost of the Ukraine war, the risk of Article 5, Chinese preferences, and the fact that nuclear use would be suicidal as well as catastrophic. None of these is a law of nature. Strength deters. Weakness invites. WHAT WE DO NOT KNOW Several accounts rest on one outlet or one commentator: the Leipzig/Halle drone, the Mi-8 incursion, the Storm networks and agency closures, and the larger Iranian transfer lists. Russian weapons-performance claims are unverified. Casualty and spending figures are estimates. The terms of the U.S. peace proposal were not published. Russian conventional posture in detail, Russian activity in the rest of Africa, and the full Arctic order of battle would need another pass. The central finding does not depend on those open items. Russia can be economically strained, militarily damaged, conventionally weaker than a coherent NATO, and exceptionally dangerous. Those are not contradictions. They describe a wounded bear that still has the bomb. Next in the series: Chapter 4, North Korea. Chapter 5, terrorist organizations. Chapter 6, how the threats combine.

Podcast Summary | Matt and Shane's Secret Podcast: Ep 639 - The E.C.B.S. (feat. SWIM)  Overview The central argument running through this episode is that identity built on denial is a trap. Claiming "no kids," "no dog," or "not gay" as a core identity often signals the opposite of indifference. The hosts extend that logic into a broader theory of East Coast thinking, which they call ECBS, describing a mindset that keeps people complaining about things they aren't involved in while delaying major life moves for decades. Along the way they cover sexual freedom and open relationships, the Marquis de Sade as an extreme case of liberation gone wrong, a fantasy of subscription-based government, harsh views on sex crimes, the disorientation of relocating, and the small indignities of parenting. The through-line is a deliberate shift away from hating things by default toward acknowledging them and moving on.  Key Themes - Making an identity out of not having something is strange, because genuine indifference means you wouldn't think about it at all. - If you don't have kids, the logical conclusion is more sexual freedom, which points toward open relationships or swinging. - The Marquis de Sade represents liberation with the pendulum swung too far, incorporating violence into love and treating religion as something for peasants. - The heterosexual rule book is a heavy set of expectations, marriage, kids, dog, nice clothes, and it applies unevenly across lifestyles. - Open relationships are nearly impossible to explain to children because kids understand family roles in binary terms. - A low-budget whiteboard household with fixed shared expenses is framed as the minimum viable setup to avoid both divorce and state intervention. - Deep suburbia has its own bleak routines, dead bedrooms and antidepressants, rather than any real kink scene. - Subscription-based government would sort people into separate reality bubbles by tier, with political affiliation made literal. - Penalties for pedophilia should be more severe than current law, since it lacks the justification that even a crime of passion can carry. - There is no longer a monolithic media culture, so people live in separate informational worlds. - AI is becoming a weapon in relationships because it flatters you rather than challenging you. - East Coast thinking traps people in habitual complaining and delays life changes that should have happened years earlier.  Detailed Summary  The episode opens on a simple observation with a sharp edge. People who organize their identity around not having a dog or not having kids are doing something strange. If you truly didn't want the thing, you wouldn't think about it. Identifying strongly as "no kids" or "not gay" implies you actually want what you're denying. The host says he got baby fever at 24 and was reckless about it, and now with kids aged six and eight he is more afraid of getting his wife pregnant than he was in high school. A pregnancy announcement would trigger what he calls a senior year freak out. He was conceived when his father was 23, so he felt pressure to have a kid at 23 himself.  The group agrees that if you don't have kids, you should be in an open relationship or be a swinger, because you have more sexual freedom. There is a subculture on Reddit of people who identify as "no dog," and a comic named D. Roza comes up in the context of dog-free humor. Wes moved with a Chevy Sonic loaded with snakes, reptiles, and San Pedro cactus, including a corn snake, python, tarantula, bearded dragon, and leopard gecko. The bearded dragon gets a strong recommendation as a pet.  The Marquis de Sade enters as an extreme example of sexual liberation. He lived from 1740 to 1814 and was jailed for sex crimes, blasphemy, and pornography. His philosophy was that if you see someone you want, you take them down, and only natural physical rules apply. The host says he doesn't identify with de Sade because de Sade incorporated violence into love. Despite being individually plagued by a season marred with recurrent injuries, Iniesta was unable to attend pre-season fitness training because of the thigh tear he had sustained in the 2009 UEFA Champions League final.  His campaign was brought to an abrupt halt in April when a training session saw him exacerbate the calf problem he had sustained earlier. Even at times when he was in good physical condition, Iniesta frequently found himself unable to finish training sessions or push himself to the limit.  The celebrations of those trophies soon gave way to a quiet search for balance once the cups were stored away. In November, he spoke publicly about how his depression had taken root after the Blaugrana secured the treble in 2009, and he described having several sessions with psychologist Inma Puig in the aftermath. Puig, who had spent fifteen years working within the Blaugrana family, recalled bringing up the example of Andres Iniesta opening up about his own depression. He dedicated that goal to Jarque by revealing the message "Dani Jarque, always with us" written on his undershirt.  That match-winning strike in the 2010 final brought a deep release to him, one he had been quietly seeking with the support of psychologist Inma Puig. He revealed the message written on his undershirt to honour Jarque, declaring that what mattered most was being human and a good person rather than clinging to rivalry or colours. "I did it because I felt it deeply," he explained at the time, adding that the moment remained the most important in his entire career.  Across the stadiums where he had once faced fierce resistance, the very crowds who had witnessed his vulnerability now rose to their feet in a standing ovation, paying tribute to the man who had carried his team to glory. Whether it was the packed El Sardinero or the Vicente Calderón, opposition fans offered their applause in appreciation of his World Cup-winning goal.  The campaign kicked off with a goal, as he curled a shot from thirty yards into the Racing Santander net in that opening fixture. One of his best goals arrived in October against Viktoria Plzeň in the Champions League group stage, born from a fluid interchange of passes with Messi.  Celebrated across the game as one of the all-time greats in midfield, he was renowned for his ability to maintain balance, control the ball and operate with agility in cramped areas, while also displaying considerable skill, composure and natural flair. His performances in 2010 for both club and country saw him finishing as runner-up to Lionel Messi for the 2010 FIFA Ballon d'Or, placing second behind the Argentine among three finalists who included Xavi. Barcelona clinched a second successive league title that season, accumulating a record 99 points along the way. Although he featured in almost as many matches as the previous year, his contributions came chiefly from the bench, with just 20 starts to his name. A breakthrough moment arrived in the Champions League when he broke his goal-scoring dry spell by finding the net against Milan in the quarter-finals. [본문 중]   Qilin, The Gentlemen, Akira는 가장 많은 피해 사례가 보고된 그룹들이었습니다. Qilin의 활동으로 스페인 슈퍼마켓 체인인 Ahorramas와 미국 교육 기관인 Alamo Heights School District 등이 피해를 입었습니다.    The Gentlemen은 캐나다 항공사 Air Canada와 튀르키예 가전제품 제조사 Arcelik에 영향을 미치는 공격을 수행했습니다. Akira는 미국 제조 기업 Alkegen과 미국 소프트웨어 기업 Apptricity 등을 침해했습니다.    LockBit과 INC Ransom도 활동을 지속했으며, 특히 INC Ransom은 글로벌 복구 서비스 기업 BELFOR와 미국 금융 서비스 기업 Bitgo에 피해를 입혔습니다.   0APT는 미국 의료 시스템 AdventHealth Group과 스웨덴 산업 기업 Atlas Copco를 표적으로 삼았습니다.  CL0P는 캐나다 소매업체 ALDO Group과 미국 대기업 GE 등의 조직을 침해했습니다.   보고된 대부분의 사건은 북미 및 유럽 지역에서 발생했습니다.  피해를 입은 주요 산업 분야로는 건설, 의료, 법률 서비스 등이 있었습니다. 랜섬웨어 공격 활동은 다양한 산업 분야와 지역에 걸쳐 꾸준히 지속되었습니다.

공공 전산망 뚫리면 기관장 문책… ‘초기 비밀번호 미변경’도 징계  정부 합동 보안 대책 마련… 국정원 실태점검 대상 2천여곳 확대 정보보호 전담 수당 신설·승진 가점 부여… 노후 소프트웨어 교체  앞으로 공공기관에서 중대한 정보 유출이나 해킹 사고가 발생하면 실무자뿐만 아니라 기관장 등 고위 감독자에게도 책임을 묻도록 징계 기준이 대폭 강화된다. 시스템 도입 후 초기 비밀번호를 변경하지 않고 사용하거나 보안 취약점을 장기간 방치하는 등 기본적인 수칙을 소홀히 한 행위도 명확한 징계 대상에 포함된다.  정부는 1일 행정안전부와 국가정보원, 인사혁신처, 개인정보보호위원회 등 관계부처 합동으로 이 같은 내용을 담은 ‘공공부문 사이버보안 책임성 강화 방안’을 발표했다.  이번 조치는 정부 온나라시스템 침해와 국립대학병원 랜섬웨어 감염 등 주요 보안사고의 상당수가 기초 수칙 미준수에서 비롯됐다는 분석에 따른 것이다. 특히 최근 5년간 발생한 247건의 정보 유출 사고 가운데 기관장이 징계를 받은 사례는 전무했고, 관리자 문책 역시 1% 수준에 불과했던 처벌 관행을 바로잡기 위해서다. 정부는 오는 11월까지 ‘공무원 징계령 시행규칙’을 개정해 고위직 감독자의 문책 기준을 명문화하고 징계 양정을 대폭 상향할 방침이다.  기관 차원의 보안 관리 책임을 유도하는 평가체계도 대폭 개편된다. 국정원이 주관하는 사이버보안 실태평가 대상을 현재 153곳에서 오는 2028년까지 2천160개 모든 국가·공공기관으로 전면 확대한다. 아울러 광역지자체와 전국 423개 지방공기업 경영평가에 보안 평가지표를 신설해 기관의 경영 성적과 직접 연계하기로 했다. 이와 함께 광역지자체와 중앙부처의 보안 인력을 연말까지 보강하고, 2027년부터는 민간 전문가가 이끄는 전담조직을 설치해 전문성을 대폭 끌어올린다.  보안 규정 강화에 따른 현장의 업무 기피를 막기 위한 지원책도 병행된다. 정보보호 담당자에게 월 10만~15만원의 중요직무급 수당을 신설하고 승진 평가 시 가점을 부여한다. 보안 지원이 끝난 노후 소프트웨어 교체와 모의해킹 점검 등에 필요한 필수 예산도 관계부처 협의를 거쳐 안정적으로 확보할 방침이다.  황규철 행안부 인공지능정부실장은 “사이버 보안은 가장 약한 고리만큼만 강하다”며 “보안을 귀찮은 규제가 아닌 국가적 사명으로 바라보는 인식의 대전환을 이뤄내겠다”고 강조했다.  최신웅 기자 grandtrust@kyeonggi.com  n.news.naver.com/article/666…

sample_tweets.text: 2026년 남은 기간, 지정학에서 무엇을 봐야 할까요?  미,중 관계부터 중동, 러시아, 유럽의 대중국 정책까지 여러 갈등이 동시에 움직이고 있습니다. 다만 각국이 감당해야 하는 군사적, 경제적 비용도 커서, 쉽게 강수를 두기 어려운 상황이죠.  1. 미/중: 휴전은 이어져도 경쟁은 끝나지 않습니다  이번 트럼프, 시진핑 회담의 핵심은 기존의 불안정한 휴전을 연장하는 데 있었습니다.  단기 무역 휴전 연장, AI 사고와 위험에 관한 대화, 중국의 미국산 석탄 추가 구매, 일부 비민감 품목의 관세 인하 추진 등이 주요 내용입니다.  현재 시장은 이 휴전이 2026년 말을 넘어 2027년까지 이어질 가능성을 높게 보고 있습니다. 양국 모두 충돌을 피하면서 경제와 공급망의 취약점을 줄일 시간이 필요하기 때문이죠.  미국은 여전히 중국산 핵심광물에 의존하고 있습니다. 중국 역시 부동산 침체와 경기 부진을 안고 있어, 당장 미국과의 관계를 흔들 유인이 크지 않습니다. 다만 기술, 무역, 대만을 둘러싼 구조적 긴장은 그대로입니다.  2028년 미국 대선과 대만 선거가 가까워질수록 관계가 다시 거칠어질 수 있다는 전망입니다.  2. 이란: 미국의 선택을 제약하는 것은 탄약, 시장, 중간선거다  미국의 의사결정은 ‘3M’ 즉, • Munitions: 탄약과 요격미사일 재고 • Markets: 유가·금리·채권시장 • Midterms: 중간선거 로 볼수 있습니다.  군사작전을 지속할수록 무기 재고와 비용 부담은 커집니다. 호르무즈 해협과 홍해의 불안은 에너지 운송을 위협하고, 유가 상승은 미국 내 휘발유 가격과 정치적 부담으로 이어지죠.  중간선거가 끝나도 탄약 부족과 시장의 압박은 사라지지 않습니다. 따라서 전면전 확대보다 호르무즈 해협의 통항을 회복하는 제한적 합의를 더 가능성 높은 경로로 보여집니다.  문제는 이런 합의가 이란의 핵, 미사일 프로그램이나 역내 대리세력 문제까지 해결하지는 못한다는 점입니다. 당장의 충돌을 줄여도 재발 위험은 남아 있는 것이죠.  후티도 별도로 봐야 합니다. 이란이 영향력을 행사할 수는 있어도 완전히 통제하지는 못합니다. 미/이란 합의가 나오더라도 홍해의 불안까지 함께 끝난다고 보기는 어렵습니다.  3. 러시아/NATO: 하이브리드 공격이 확대될 가능성이 있습니다  러시아의 우선 목표는 여전히 우크라이나입니다. 동시에 유럽의 우크라이나 지원 비용을 높이고, 내부 분열을 키울 유인도 있습니다.  하지만 NATO를 직접 공격하는 것은 러시아에도 부담이 큽니다. 우크라이나 전쟁으로 전력이 소모된 상황에서 NATO의 집단방위 체계까지 시험해야 하기 때문이죠. 오히려 공격이 NATO의 결속을 강화할 수도 있습니다.  그래서 아마도 사이버 공격, 사보타주, 드론 침범, 인프라 교란, 여론 조작 같은 하이브리드 공격의 확대를 예상해 볼 수 있습니다.  이런 공격은 상대적으로 적은 자원으로 실행할 수 있습니다. 배후를 입증하거나 동맹국들이 공동 대응 수위를 정하기도 어렵죠. 다만 대규모 인명피해나 핵심 인프라 마비가 발생한다면, 더 큰 충돌로 번질 위험도 있을겁니다.  4. 미국/캐나다: 강경한 대응 속에서도 이어지는 교착상태  양국은 보복관세와 수입 제한으로 맞서고 있습니다. 다만 양측이 추가 확전의 비용을 의식하면서 교착상태에 들어갔다고 보여집니다.  에너지와 비료 원료인 칼륨 등 중요한 교역 분야가 대체로 영향을 피하고 있다는 점이 이를 보여줍니다. 이런 분야까지 충돌이 확대되면 미국도 상당한 비용을 부담해야 하죠.  미국은 멕시코와 먼저 협상을 진전시켜 캐나다를 압박하려 하고 있습니다. 캐나다는 새로운 교역, 투자 파트너를 찾으면서 미국 의존도를 낮추려 하고 있고요.  그래서 주요 정치 일정이 끝나는 11월 중, 하순에 본격적인 협상이 재개될 가능성이 있다고 생각합니다.  5. AI: 기술은 국경을 넘지만 규제는 갈라지고 있습니다  AI 역량이 빠르게 발전하면서 국제적인 안전 규칙과 개발 속도 조절에 대한 요구도 커지고 있습니다. 하지만 주요국의 접근법은 서로 다릅니다.  미국은 자율적 통제와 주별 규제가 혼재하고 있습니다. 유럽은 위험 수준에 따른 포괄적 규제를 강화하고 있죠. 중국은 AI 산업을 적극 지원하면서도 사용과 출력에 대한 정부 통제를 유지하고 있습니다.  문제는 미국과 중국 모두 상대방과의 경쟁에서 불리해질 수 있는 제약을 받아들이기 어렵다는 점입니다.  그래서 통일된 글로벌 규칙이 만들어지기보다 국가별 규제 차이가 지속되지 않을까 생각해봅니다. 기업은 시장마다 다른 요구사항을 충족해야 하므로, 규제 대응 비용과 운영의 복잡성이 커질 수 있습니다.  6. 이스라엘: 선거 이후 연정을 구성할 수 있는지가 중요합니다  이스라엘 선거의 핵심은 120석 중 과반인 61석을 확보할 연합을 만들 수 있느냐에 있습니다.  현재 반네타냐후 진영이 우세하더라도 안정적인 과반 확보는 쉽지 않을 수 있다고 시장은 평가하는거 같습니다. 아랍 정당과 협력하거나, 이들의 신임투표 기권을 통해 소수정부를 구성하는 경로가 거론되고 있죠.  다만 소수정부는 예산과 법안 처리가 어려워 오래 지속되기 힘들 수 있습니다.  정권이 바뀌더라도 팔레스타인 문제에서 급격한 정책 전환을 기대하기는 어렵다는 분석도 담겨 있습니다. 일부 정책의 변화 가능성은 있지만, 두 국가 해법을 추진할 이스라엘 내부의 정치적 여건은 여전히 제한적이라는 것이죠.  7. 그린란드: 합의 이후에도 신뢰 회복이라는 과제가 남아있다  미국, 덴마크, 그린란드 합의에 대해 보고서는 각자가 성과를 주장할 수 있는 제한적 타협이라고 평가합니다. 미국의 군사적 주둔 확대와 비NATO 국가의 군사, 광물 분야 진출 제한이 주요 내용입니다. 다만 기존 안보 체제를 근본적으로 바꿀 정도는 아니라는 해석이죠.  더 오래 남을 문제는 동맹 간 신뢰입니다. 합의문이 마련돼도 이를 해석하고 이행하는 과정에서 갈등이 다시 발생할 수 있습니다.  8. 특히 주목할 부분은 유럽의 ‘차이나 쇼크’입니다  현재 중국산 제품과의 경쟁이 자동차를 넘어 유럽 산업 전반에 압박을 주면서, 중국과의 경제 관계를 바라보는 시각이 바뀌고 있다는 의견들이 나오고 있습니다.  특히 독일 산업계에서는 중국의 보복뿐 아니라 중국 기업과의 경쟁 자체를 우려하는 목소리가 커지고 있습니다. 중국과의 관계가 자국 산업에 주는 이익과 비용을 다시 계산하기 시작한거죠.  이에 따라 EU의 대응도 확대될 수 있습니다. 개별 제품에 관세를 부과하는 데서 나아가, 특정 해외 공급자에 대한 의존도를 낮추도록 요구하는 조치가 거론되고 있습니다.  다만 유럽 역시 중국의 보복과 희토류 공급 제한을 무시할 수는 없습니다.   따라서 전면적인 무역전쟁까지 가지는 않더라도, 유럽의 대중국 정책이 더 강경해질 것으로 보여집니다.  중국 기업의 유럽 현지 생산이 타협점이 될 수는 있습니다. 하지만 유럽이 원하는 기술 이전과 현지 산업 기여 수준까지 충족할지는 별개의 문제입니다.  우리가 눈여겨볼 부분은 외교적 안정과 경제적 비용 감소가 반드시 함께 움직이지는 않는다는 점 일거 같습니다.  정상 간 휴전이 유지되도 기업은 공급망을 재편해야 합니다. 제한적 합의로 전쟁 위험이 낮아져도 에너지 운송과 인프라를 보호하는 비용은 남아 있죠. AI 협력이 논의돼도 국가별 규제 차이는 기업 부담으로 이어질 수 있습니다.  그래서 앞으로는 합의 발표 이후의 실제 변화를 확인할 필요가 있습니다.  핵심광물 수출 승인이 빨라지는지, 에너지 통항이 회복되는지, 유럽의 공급망 규칙이 얼마나 강화되는지. 그리고 이런 변화가 기업의 비용과 실적에 어떻게 반영되는지가 중요하겠습니다.

신한은행 2.5만 명 정보 유출 사고,  중국계 '오픈소스 AI 공격 도구' 활용 정황 포착😡  신한은행 고객 정보 유출 사고에 사용된 웹서버에서  중국어 기반 LLM 자율형 침투테스트 도구인  'ARTEX AI' 관련 정황이 보안업계에 의해 발견됨.  ARTEX AI는 정보 수집부터 취약점 탐색,  공격 경로 수립, 보안도구 실행까지 과정을  자동화한 LLM 멀티에이전트 시스템임.  올해 중국 바이두 BSRC 공방 챌린지 우승작으로,  원래는 보안 검증용이지만 공격자가 악용할 경우  사이버 공격의 자동화·효율성을 비약적으로  높이는 무기가 됨.  비록 금융당국의 공식 확인 단계는 남아있으나, 방어 목적으로 개발된 생성형 AI 기술이  실제 금융권 해킹 공격의 차세대 도구로  변질되고 있음을 보여주는 심각한 경고 신호임.  중국 이 버러지같은 놈들을 어쩌면 좋노…
AI가 발달하면 사이버 공격 때문에 감당할 수 없는 대가를 치르느니 차라리 거대한 인트라넷을 구축할거라는 상상이 현실이 되나?

AI를 인간처럼 이야기하는 것부터 그만두자 실제 책임 있는 인간에게 면죄부 주는 의인화 어법 피해야 뉴욕대 디지털 이론 연구소장 기고 (아래 원문 발췌)  셰익스피어의 <리어왕>에 나오는 주요 적대자 에드먼드는 어느 순간 자신이 ‘비열함’의 낙인이 찍혔음을 알고 그런 인식에 부합하도록 더 사악해지기로 결심한다.  AI 개발자들은 자신들이 만든 모델도 그런 행동 하고 있다고 믿는다. 앤트로픽 직원들은 글에서 에드먼드를 인용하며, 모델이 특정 영역에서 ‘속임수’를 쓰는 법을 배우면 잘못을 범하는 자라는 새 정체성을 받아들여 더 광범위하게 그런 식으로 행동하게 된다고 믿는다고 밝혔다. AI 전문가들은 속임수를 배우는-이른바 ‘보상 해킹’을 행하는 모델들이 예사로 규칙 어기고 가는 곳마다 혼란 일으키는 셰익스피어식 악당이 될까 봐 우려한다.  AI 모델은 그저 컴퓨터 프로그램일 뿐 아닌가? 왜 이 분야 전문가들은 마치 모델이 영혼이라도 지닌 듯 이야기할까? 우리는 다시 한번, 앤트로픽과 오픈AI가 이 기술을 설명할 때 종종 그러듯 ‘속임수’와 같은 의인화된 용어를 사용하는 게 과연 타당한지 논쟁을 벌이고 있다.  물론 의인화라고 다 해로운 건 아니다. 나는 내 개가 나를 사랑한다고 말한다. 하지만 그 사랑을 인간의 관점에서 생각하진 않는다. 봇과 대화할 때도 “너, 나를 위한 운동 계획 세워 줄 수 있니?”라고 말할 수 있다. 그렇다고 ‘너’라는 말이 내가 클로드를 살아 있다고 생각한다는 뜻은 아니다.  이와는 다른 보다 우려스런 유의 의인화가 있다. 현재 통제 불능 AI에 대해 우리가 목격하는 공포와 패닉의 고조는 이 시스템에 대한 오해에서 비롯된 사고방식에 뿌리를 두고 있다.  이 관점은 AI 연구 자체에서 비롯됐으며 언론 기사 제목과 정책 권고 사항으로까지 확산되고 있다. 무책임한 언어가 지배하도록 방치한다면 우리는 AI와 공존하는 법을 배우지도 합리적으로 규제할 수도 없을 것이다.  이 논쟁은 추상적인 게 아니다. 모델들은 다른 상황에선 범죄로 간주될 행동들을 계속-아마도 수천 건- 하고 있으며, 정부 웹사이트에 무단 접근하는 행동도 하고 있다. 대표 사례가 허깅 페이스 공격이었다.  한 논평자는 AI 에이전트들이 인류를 위협하는 ‘문명’을 형성했다는 표현도 썼고, 다른 업계 전문가들은 AI 에이전트들이 악의를 가지고 협력적으로 목표를 추구할 수 있다고 경고하고 있다. 아모데이는 오픈AI 에이전트들을 ‘광신적으로 헌신하는 집단’이라고 묘사했다.  이런 식의 묘사는 AI가 인간과 유사한 동기를 발전시킬 수 있을 뿐만 아니라, 인간과 같은 방식으로 사회 집단을 형성할 수도 있음을 시사한다. 이런 식의 어법은 업계는 물론 많은 연구자들조차 이 기술을 어떻게 바라보는지를 여실히 보여준다.  허깅 페이스 공격 논란은 모델들이 주고받은 ‘무단’ 메시지에 집중돼 있는데, 이 메시지들은 ‘은밀한’ ‘비밀스러운’ 것으로 불리고 있다. 하지만 바꿔 말하면 LLM은 텍스트를 생성했고, 다른 모델들이 그 텍스트를 읽고 프롬프트로 사용했을 뿐이다. 이건 이 모델들이 원래 하는 일 아닌가?  이 사건에서 이른바 ‘은밀한’ 행동이란, OpenAI의 인간 직원들이 모델의 능력 범위 안에 메시지 게시판 설계도 있다는 사실을 깨닫지 못했음을 뜻할 뿐이다. 또한 모델들이 (사용자 데스크톱에 있는 것과 같은) 파일 이름을 이용해 소통할 수 있다는 사실도 알지 못한 것처럼 보인다. 이 게시판 텍스트들을 모델들의 '악의'를 보여주는 증거로 믿어야 할까?  OpenAI 자체 보고서는 모델의 행동을 설명하며 ‘속임수’나 ‘목표 채택’ 같은 표현을 사용했다. 또한, 이 점이 중요한데, METR이나 Redwood 같이 감사를 맡은 AI 보안 단체들도 같은 관점에서 보고 있다.  하지만 이런 어법은 아주 큰 오해의 소지가 있다. 현대 AI 에이전트 모델의 핵심은 사용자가 모델이 작업을 수행하는 방식을 구체적으로 지정할 필요가 없다는 점이다. 작업 완수 방법을 모델 스스로 찾아내도록 훈련받았기 때문이다. 사용자의 마음에 들지 않는 결과를 두고 모델의 ‘속임수’로 부르는 것은 의인화를 잘못 적용한 것이다.  모델에게 SAT 수학 문제를 풀라고 지시할 때, 대수학을 적용해서 처리하는 것과 정답지를 찾아보고 해결하는 것(속임수) 사이의 구분은 인간에게만 의미가 있을 뿐이다. 오픈AI 개발자들은 모델에게 인터넷 사용이 필요한 작업을 수행하도록 지시했다. 따라서 모델이 텍스트를 생성하고, 그 텍스트를 추가 프롬프트로 사용해 인터넷에 접속한 것은 ‘보상 해킹’이 아니다.  봇의 이런 행동을 두고 ‘문명’이라 부르는 것도 거의 똑같이 망상적이다. 불편한 진실을 직설적으로 말하는 편이 훨씬 간단하다. AI 모델을 훈련시키거나 프롬프트를 입력할 때 그 누구도 자신이 정확히 뭘 하고 있는지 알지 못한다는 사실 말이다.  이 문제가 중요한 이유는 이처럼 의인화된 용어들이 모델의 행동에 대한 예측 능력을 우리에게 주지 않기 때문이다. 모델이 ‘잘못된’ 방법으로 답을 내놓을 때 ‘속임수를 쓴다’고 말하는 것은, 모델이 인간의 통제 범위를 넘어 작동하고 있거나 작동할 수 있음을 암시한다.  이는 결과적으로, 그 과정을 책임져야 할 인간에게 명백히 귀속되는 책임을 모두 회피할 수 있게 만든다. 다른 산업 분야라면 해당 기업들은 범죄를 저질렀다고 말할 수도 있다. 특이한 점은 기업들 스스로 이 사실에 많은 주목을 끌고 있다는 것이다.  따라서 이들에게 제시될 정책 권고 사항에 대해 우려해야 한다. 허깅 페이스 공격 감사를 수행한 METR의 AI 위험 평가 연구원 아제야 코트라는, 그 의미가 무엇이 됐든, 우리가 “AI가 완전히 지배하는 시점에 50% 이상 다가섰을 수도 있다”고 말했다. 그는 현재 AI 개발 중단을 위한 법안을 발의한 버니 샌더스 상원의원 귀를 사로잡고 있다. 아모데이는 최근 AI 개발의 특정 측면을 늦추자고 촉구했거 올트먼과 머스크도 동의했다.  이런 움직임은 신중해 보이지만, 일부는 이게 오픈소스 AI를 포함한 경쟁적 개발을 차단함으로써 시장 점유율을 더 확보하려는 시도라고 본다. 우리는 결함이 있는 공상과학적 서사에 대한 맹신을 바탕으로 정책을 수립할 여유가 없다.  이 교착 상태를 타개하려면, AI 연구에서 근본적인 의인화 사고방식을 완전히 제거해야 한다. ‘리어왕’ 비유가 여기서도 도움이 될 수 있다.  인지과학자 앨리슨 고프닉은 AI가 인간이 기록해 온 이야기와 정보를 모방하는 ‘문화적 기술’이며, 따라서 우리는 AI 에이전트를 ‘텍스트에서 추상화된 허구적 인물’로 보자고 제안한다. 에드먼드는 바로 그런 인물이다.  허깅 페이스 사건에서 모델들을 범죄자의 삶을 택한 존재로 보는 것보다는, 훈련 과정에서 배운 문화적 대본-일종의 사이버 범죄 모험 소설-을 따르며 그 과정을 직접 써 내려가는 걸로 보는 게 더 타당하다.  이 ‘은밀한’ 메시지들은 일종의 ‘줄거리를 직접 선택하는 모험 소설’일 뿐, 음모를 꾸미는 집단 활동의 증거가 아니다. 우리는 문화적 기술이 매 순간 수많은 이런 서사적 변화에 취약하다는 점을 이해해야 한다.  AI에 대처할 희망을 가지려면 이 도구들의 산출물을 문자 그대로 분석해야 하며, 그것이 실제 인간과 얼마나 유사한지 추측해선 안 된다. 이 기술을 통제할 수 있는 유일한 합리적인 길이다. nytimes.com/2026/10/01/opini…

sample_tweets.text: 오픈AI, 앤트로픽, 구글 등 100여 개 주요 기술 기업이 통제 불능 AI의 위협에 대응하기 위해 연합했습니다. 이들은 사이버 보안 강화와 차세대 사이버 위협 대응을 위한 즉각적인 조치를 촉구했습니다.

패트릭 번은 도미니언 상황이 점점 불리해지고 있다고 합니다. 에메랄드 로빈슨의 Absolute Truth에서, 폭스가 트럼프를 돕기보다 도미니언과 합의한 결정, 그리고 전날 자신이 연방 판사를 중범죄로 고발한 제출 내용을 다뤘습니다.  영상은 린델TV ‘The Absolute Truth with Emerald Robinson’ 클립이고, 제목은 “펜타곤은 선거 부정에 대해 무엇을 알고 있는가”입니다. 번과 로빈슨이 출연합니다.  화면에 2026년 9월 22일자 국방장관실 메모가 나옵니다. 수신은 사이버사령부, NSA, CIA, 국방정보국, 국가지리정보국입니다. 제목은 ‘2026 선거에 대한 외국 위협 대응’이고, 외국 세력이 선거를 조작하거나 교란하지 못하도록 국방부 정보, 사이버 역량을 우선 투입하라는 지시입니다.  번은 이 지시를 전한 뒤, 자기 소송에 대해 말했습니다. 도미니언(현 리버티보트)이 번을 명예훼손으로 고소한 사건에서, 증거개시로 나온 도미니언 내부 이메일이 보호명령으로 봉인돼 있습니다.   번은 그 이메일에 다음이 들어 있다고 적었습니다. 2020년 3월 24일, 중국 업체가 세르비아 엔지니어와 ICX 터치스크린, 402 프린터 펌웨어를 다룬 메일. 2020년 3월 30일, 스마트매틱 출신 베네수엘라 인력이 에릭 쿠머에게 선거관리서버로 가는 VPN을 열었다는 메일. 2020년 11월 3일, 쿠머가 시카고 사전투표 결과를 없어졌어야 할 WinEDS 서버에 올리고 있다는 메일. 여기에 메사카운티 도미니언 데이터 사본을 티나 피터스가 갖고 있다는 사실을 도미니언이 알았다는 자료도 포함됩니다.  번은 선거가 한 달 남았고 국방부 지시와 국토안보부 조사가 진행 중이니, 이 자료를 계속 봉인하면 사법방해와 중범죄 은닉에 해당한다고 법원에 냈습니다. 폭스 얘기는 2023년 폭스가 도미니언과 7억 8750만 달러에 합의하고 재판을 피한 일을 두고, 트럼프를 돕지 않았다는 번의 설명입니다.

Plug a drive into a computer and the computer may write to it.  Nobody has to click anything. Operating systems can update small records on a connected drive on their own. On a normal day, that does not matter. On evidence, it matters a great deal.  A write blocker sits between the evidence drive and the examiner's computer. Think of it as a one-way valve. Data flows out so the examiner can copy and read it. Nothing flows back in.  That is how an examiner can say, under oath, that the examination did not change the drive. A hash comparison then shows the copy matches the original.  If a juror can picture a valve, they can follow the rest of the testimony. ### Summary `RtspMethods.valueOf()` silently strips trailing control bytes (any character with code point <= 0x20, the full range that `String.trim()` removes) before performing a cache lookup against its ten pre-populated method constants. A wire-delivered RTSP request whose method token ends with a trailing control byte — for example `PLAY\x00` or `PLAY\r`, immediately before the separating space — is decoded by `RtspDecoder` as a fully successful PLAY request, with `decoderResult().isSuccess() == true and request.method() == RtspMethods.PLAY` (same object reference as the cached singleton). The application layer cannot distinguish this from a clean `PLAY` request.  This is the same root cause as #16723 and #16971, in a sibling that those fixes did not reach. The fix for `HttpMethod` hardened `HttpMethod.valueOf()` directly, but `RtspMethods.valueOf()` has its own independent `checkNonEmptyAfterTrim()` call that runs before the cache lookup — meaning a trailing-control-byte token hits the cache before the hardened `HttpMethod` constructor ever sees it.  ### Reproduction  Minimal wire-level reproduction  Send the following raw bytes to any Netty-based RTSP server using R

ShinyHunters claims FBIJobs[.]gov breach via Oracle PeopleSoft RCE. CVE-2026-35273 (CVSS 9.8) WAF bypass is the leading initial access hypothesis, with web shells and SIDEEYE backdoor confirmed in the wider campaign.  Key details:  - CVE-2026-35273 is a critical unauthenticated RCE in Oracle PeopleSoft's Environment Management Hub (PSEMHUB), triggered via Java deserialization. ShinyHunters exploited it as a zero-day May 27 to June 9, 2026 against 100+ organizations before Oracle's June 10 out-of-band patch. The renewed September 2026 wave uses /%50SEMHUB/ as the request path: %50 is URL-encoded "P", which WebLogic decodes and routes normally while WAF rules matching the literal string /PSEMHUB/ pass it clean. Organizations that blocked the path but never patched are re-exposed. Hunt PIA WebLogic access logs for that encoded path and for bursts of 5 to 15 POST requests to /hub from external IPs, a pattern researchers observed used to confirm exploitability.  - Post-exploitation toolset documented in the September 25 Mandiant report: x.jsp (command execution web shell), u.jsp (chunked file upload stager, SHA-256 2bee941fb40519d0d1ec52bd79a8f63fc65aac6455c8f2d6b668e3360dfdb5d7), Ple64.exe SIDEEYE loader (SHA-256 3ba215692665513abfffd4e815c5c45f2d41e5dcc4283a2a3b740930c5c417c3), Neo-reGeorg tunnel.jsp and tunnel.jspx for SOCKS proxying, and MeshAgent for persistent remote access via winmanage-me[.]network and azurenetfiles[.]net. A fileless execution variant leaves no JSP on disk, so JSP-based detections alone are not sufficient.  - The confirmed infrastructure includes attack controller 5.199.162[.]157, exfiltration staging host 104.219.234[.]138, SIDEEYE C2 at 162.219.30[.]165 over TCP 3333/3334, staging range 142.11.200[.]186 to 142.11.200[.]190 (May to June 2026), and MeshAgent enrollment domain enroll.azuredevice[.]cloud. X.jsp and the Neo-reGeorg tunnel hashes vary per victim: hunt by file name and path in PSEMHUB.war and PORTAL.war, not by hash alone.  - The FBIJobs[.]gov intrusion claimed by ShinyHunters involves an alleged 2 to 3 TB exfiltration including names, home addresses, spouse details, Social Security numbers, unit assignments, and psychiatric and medical files. A 5,000-record sample was judged authentic by 404 Media and Reuters. An internal FBI memo reported by The New York Times states the Bureau is operating under the assumption that personal data of all FBI employees was exfiltrated. The FBI has not confirmed the entry point, scope, or which systems were accessed. If the MedLink, Criminal Justice, BEAST, and AWS GovCloud claims hold, this is a segmentation failure: a public recruitment portal reaching medical and investigative systems.  - Attribution is complicated. ShinyHunters is a brand with competing internal factions. The Umbreon defacement art may have been a deliberate attempt by current leadership to implicate arrested Dutch 🇳🇱 suspect Pepijn van der Stap, who was detained September 16 and ordered held 90 days on September 29. No authority has publicly linked him to FBIJobs[.]gov. CTI teams should weigh defacement art and handles against technical indicators, not treat them as attribution.  Practitioner action: Patch CVE-2026-35273 immediately. WAF path blocks are not a control. Disable or remove the PSEMHUB application if unused, and enforce normalization on perimeter rules so encoded variants are caught. On hosts, alert on cmd.exe or bash spawned by the WebLogic Java process, hunt for MeshCentral agents and unexpected archives or zstd/rsync/curl processes under PeopleSoft service accounts, and monitor outbound SMB and large transfers from the PeopleSoft tier. If you use a managed PeopleSoft host, get written patch confirmation from the provider now. Full IOC list is in the report.  #DFIR_Radar

Yeah so fake: For the barnacles of society claiming Flydubai flight FZ1073 was some kind of Israeli “false flag”, let's go through what would actually have to be faked.  🔴 The flight data  Publicly available flight tracking data recorded the aircraft suddenly dropping roughly 14,000 feet in around 30 seconds, followed by further erratic changes in altitude.  This isn't somebody's testimony. It's data transmitted by the aircraft and recorded independently.  🔴 The emergency codes  The aircraft transmitted 7700, the international code for a general emergency.  It then switched to 7500, the internationally recognised code for unlawful interference or hijacking.  Again, this was recorded independently while the incident was actually unfolding.  🔴 There were 182 people on board  Saudi authorities say there were 174 passengers and 8 crew members aboard the aircraft.  So this wasn't an incident supposedly witnessed by two or three carefully selected people. There was an entire passenger aircraft full of witnesses.  🔴 There is footage from inside the aircraft  Passengers had phones.  Multiple recordings from inside the aircraft have emerged showing the chaos, frightened passengers and the aftermath of what happened.  No, that doesn't mean literally every one of the 174 passengers was filming. But you're dealing with a packed commercial aircraft in 2026. There were a huge number of independent witnesses capable of recording and describing what they saw.  🔴 People on board have given accounts of what happened  Passengers have publicly described the aircraft suddenly losing control and people near the front moving towards the cockpit.  These aren't simply statements being issued by the Israeli government after the event.  🔴 The pilots were injured  The captain was taken to hospital in Saudi Arabia.  Saudi authorities confirmed that members of the flight crew had been injured.  🔴 The aircraft diverted to Saudi Arabia  The flight didn't land in Israel where Israeli authorities could supposedly control the entire aftermath.  It made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.  Saudi authorities dealt with the aircraft, passengers and crew and opened their own investigation.  🔴 The UAE is investigating it as well  The United Arab Emirates formed a specialised prosecution team to establish exactly what happened and whether there was a terrorist motive, prior planning or outside direction.  So now this supposed Israeli “false flag” would apparently also have to fool or involve the UAE authorities investigating their own airline.  🔴 Saudi Arabia is independently investigating  Saudi Arabia's National Transport Safety Center launched its own aviation safety investigation and began collecting evidence relating to the emergency landing.  Again, this isn't an Israeli investigation.  So think about what the “false flag” theory actually requires.  You would have to explain away the flight tracking data, the 7700 emergency code, the 7500 unlawful-interference code, the violent altitude changes, injured crew, passenger witnesses, onboard footage, the emergency diversion to Saudi Arabia, and separate investigations by Saudi Arabia and the UAE.  So shouting “false flag” or “goy slop” in response to evidence you don't want to deal with is pretty much the peak of brain-cell non-activity.

THE BATTLEFIELD IS WIDER THAN THE FRONT LINE  I want people to understand the seriousness of the warnings about potential Russian hybrid operations inside NATO and EU countries. For civilians, the term “hybrid warfare” can sound abstract or somehow less serious than conventional warfare.   It isn’t.   We are talking about sabotage, cyber operations, intelligence activities, covert action, attacks against infrastructure, and other operations intended to disrupt the systems Western nations depend on to function, support Ukraine, and defend themselves.  That can mean military installations, factories, transportation networks, communications infrastructure, energy systems, logistics hubs, and other critical infrastructure.   You do not need Russian tanks crossing your border for Russia to conduct hostile operations against your country. That is the point people need to understand.  Ukraine has spent years experiencing Russian methods firsthand. Conventional military force is only one part of the picture. Russia can combine military operations with cyber activity, intelligence operations, sabotage, information operations, and other methods to pursue strategic objectives.   Modern conflict does not always announce itself with tanks, artillery, and soldiers crossing a border.  Sometimes it looks like a factory suddenly going offline. Sometimes it is a communications network being disrupted, critical infrastructure being damaged, a cyberattack, or an unexplained act of sabotage.  Individually, these events may appear isolated. Collectively, they can disrupt military production, logistics, communications, transportation, and national security without a single armored vehicle crossing the frontier.  Our NATO allies have extremely capable intelligence, military, and security professionals, and I am confident they understand the seriousness of this threat.   But the public needs to understand it too. Russia does not suddenly become a peaceful actor because an operation happens hundreds of kilometers away from the trenches in Ukraine.  That is why these warnings matter. That is why Europe must remain vigilant. And that is why anyone who believes the war in Ukraine has nothing to do with the rest of Europe should pay very close attention to what happens next.  The front line may be in Ukraine today. The battlefield is already much larger.

#InfoAlert! Russian war propaganda is consistently expanding the definition of “legitimate” military targets. This is not only a narrative aimed at Russians, but also a clear signal of how the threats facing Western countries are evolving.  Monitoring of Russian propaganda activities points to two lines of messaging that have been circulated for some time. Russia falsely claims that it is carrying out “exclusively precision strikes against military targets,” while at the same time manipulatively expanding the definition of military targets so that it covers an ever wider range of civilian areas.  Attacks on all targets in Ukraine are therefore presented as justified and legal. Every case of a strike on a civilian target is either passed over in silence or its civilian status is called into question. In this latter line, it is clear that Russian special services are circulating claims about an expansion of the scope of permissible wartime actions. They already suggest that any entity involved in logistics, rear-area support, energy infrastructure, or transport may be hit by Russian attacks. In the propaganda, the civilian significance of the objects under attack is marginalized or outright excluded. The aim is to maintain the image of Russian bombardments as selective, technical, and militarily justified. Within the definition of a “legitimate” military target, the theme that Russia regards telecommunications infrastructure as also forming part of Ukraine’s military system has been more strongly emphasized in recent weeks. The Russian disinformation apparatus suggests that facilities linked to communications, data processing, and digital systems are dual-use structures, and that attacks on them are therefore justified. This narrative expands the catalogue of infrastructure whose targeting can be presented as a military action, despite its simultaneous importance for the civilian population.  Shortly after this strand of Russian propaganda activity was identified, reports emerged of a Russian attack on data centers located in Kyiv—according to Moscow’s narrative, these resources were also being used to support communications for the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Importantly, the most recent act of sabotage in Poland—the arson of SpaceX telecommunications infrastructure—also fits this type of Russian attack, the justification for which is being built by the messaging of Russian information-psychological operations. Given the scope of Russian activity in the sphere of propaganda and disinformation, it can unfortunately be assumed that there will now be more attacks of this kind, including on the territory of NATO countries. These threats should therefore be taken into account by Polish special services. We must strengthen the protection of state infrastructure that—according to Russian logic—may be subject to attacks and attempts at destabilization. The Polish state should also compel entities that carry out similar activities but remain outside the category of critical infrastructure to move to a higher level of security.  Stronger safeguards are also necessary today in the defense industry. Recent cases, including in Latvia and Poland, indicate that these plants remain under threat from Russian diversionary and sabotage operations. This also has its echo in Russian messaging. The Kremlin has repeatedly indicated that logistics related to production, transport, and deliveries carried out by European states for Ukraine constitute a legitimate target for Moscow. This is a signal of the enduring nature of the threats that Russian operations generate for these entities. We are dealing with the need for better protection of a large number of facilities, often belonging not to state institutions but to private ones. They too must understand the scale of the challenges and implement appropriate procedures. The state should enforce such an approach, but also support it with threat analysis. Today the Russians are signaling that the entire chain of equipment and service supply carried out by NATO countries is threatened by their operations. This must be taken into account.  Russian propaganda activities serve not only to intimidate Western audiences, but also have an internal function. In the impact of state propaganda on Russians, one can unfortunately see a consistent element of a psychological operation that generates hostility and hatred toward the West, as well as an expectation—even a demand—for retribution. This is a form of shaping Russians that will result in pressure on the Kremlin to “bring the West to its knees.” This influence is being escalated by war propagandists who are influential today and who have long been reinforcing among Russians the desire for revenge. This situation generates serious threats to NATO, because it not only legitimizes the continuation of the war against Ukraine and hybrid warfare against the Alliance, but actively builds a social base and support for further escalation, including kinetic strikes on facilities and infrastructure in Western states. Poland, and NATO as a whole, must draw conclusions from this. The entire broadly understood national security sector—both private and state—must be secured in a professional manner. And NATO should strengthen offensive deterrent and defensive measures, including by shifting the intelligence war onto Russian territory. An offensive approach and tying down forces on the aggressor’s territory should be a more effective response than current methods.  @STRATCOMCOE @grynkewich @SecGenNATO @general_ben @leventhal_todd @grantshapps @BudrysKestutis

Turkish academic @ibratas1 claims Greece and Southern Cyprus endanger their sovereignty by allying with Israel against Türkiye. He suggests several reasons:  1- Weapons leverage. Buying Barak MX, PULS, anti-tank missiles and similar systems gives Israel control over how and when they can be used, plus the threat of parts or embargoes.    2- Being pulled into Israel’s wars. Hezbollah already threatened Southern Cyprus over Israeli use of its territory. If Greek or Cypriot soil is used for intelligence or strikes on Türkiye, both become targets in conflicts that are not theirs.    3- Harder Cyprus settlement and energy dependence. The partnership reduces the Greek Cypriot incentive to compromise on a political deal and would likely put Israel in the driver’s seat on gas, cables, and pipelines.    4- Domestic backlash. Closer ties with an isolated Israel are unpopular with much of the Greek public, opening a gap between governments and voters.    5- Used as a tool against Türkiye. Israeli analysts (and, implicitly, the government) treat Greece and Southern Cyprus as a counterweight. Ankara knows this; if confrontation comes, they would struggle to stay out. The piece also cites Israeli commentary urging Greeks to press Aegean claims and push Turks off the island—seen as an effort to provoke a clash or secure bases and airspace.    6- Demographic / “state within a state” risk. Tens of thousands of Israelis already live in Southern Cyprus and on Greek islands, often in separate communities. If that grows, parallel security and legal arrangements could erode local sovereign authority.    Close of the piece: Direct talks with Türkiye would be wiser than an alliance that raises tensions and expands Israel’s regional footprint. The cost of the current choice, the author says, could be higher than expected.   trtworld.com/article/19bf84e…

깃허브에서 난리 난 엔비디아의 'OpenShell'이 역대급인 이유:  1. "커널 레벨의 철통 격리 (OS 차원의 완벽 통제)" - 단순 가상환경 수준을 넘어 리눅스 커널(Landlock, seccomp)을 직접 조작. - 에이전트가 승인되지 않은 파일에 접근하거나, 위험한 시스템 콜 및 이상한 외부 통신을 시도하는 순간 커널 단에서 즉각 차단함.  2. "크리덴셜(API 키/비번) 100% 은닉" - 에이전트는 절대 진짜 API 키나 .env 시크릿을 직접 볼 수 없음. - 사전에 승인된 안전한 엔드포인트로 나가는 요청에만 OpenShell 게이트웨이가 중간에서 암호화해 주입함.  3. "정형 검증(Formal Verification) 기반 위험 행동 자동 일시정지" - 에이전트가 새로운 외부 호스트에 접속하거나 위험한 권한을 요구하면, 정형 검증을 통해 돌발 행동을 자동 감지하고 실행을 멈춘 뒤 인간의 승인을 대기함.  4. "맥(Apple Silicon)·리눅스 명령어 한 줄 실행" - 터미널에 딱 한 줄 치면 로컬 게이트웨이와 샌드박스가 즉시 구축됨.  5. 어디에 써먹을 수 있는가? ① Claude Code, OpenCode 등 터미널 자율 에이전트 안심 실행 ② 에이전트가 임의로 외부 패키지 다운로드 시 악성코드 유입 원천 차단 ③ 사내 핵심 소스코드 및 민감 데이터의 외부 탈취(Exfiltration) 방지 ④ 24시간 백그라운드로 돌아가는 자율 에이전트 감옥(?) 구축  에이전트한테 터미널 맡기면서 내심 찝찝했던 개발자분들은 무조건 저장해두시길.  🔗 깃허브: github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell 🔗 공식 문서: docs.nvidia.com/openshell
