Sin autem quid elegans, acutum, divinum, id totum meum est. Emendationes meas, quae passim occurrunt, ne mutaveris: emendatae enim sunt. Codices quos citavi, si non inveneris, quaere diligentius; si ne sic quidem, crede mihi. Scaligero, Casaubono, Gudgeono ceterisque obtrectatoribus nihil dico, nisi illud Flacci: Odi profanum vulgus et arceo. Vale, et me, si potes, ama; sin minus, time. Dabam ex Aedibus Magistralibus, Idibus Octobribus, Anno MDCXII. ⁂ The same, Englished for the Fellowes: Theophilus Periwinkle Hulse, Doctor of Divinity, Master of St. Polyrots' College, sends the Reader many greetings. Here, Reader, are the Memoires of my life, written not for vanity but for truth. So many falsehoods have been spread of me by my Colleagues, so many injustices by my rivals, and so many absurdities by Printers, that I thought it right that Hulse should at last speak of Hulse himself. If you meet anything in these pages that seems ill-suited to good Latin, know that it is not the Author's but the Compositor's, whom I have already dismissed down the stairs. If you find anything elegant, sharp or divine, it is entirely mine. Do not alter my emendations, which occur throughout: they are emended already. If you cannot find the manuscripts I cite, look harder; if not even then, take my word for it. To Scaliger, Casaubon, Gudgeon and my other detractors I say nothing, except that line of Horace: I hate the profane crowd and keep it at a distance. Farewell, and love me if you can; if not, fear me. Given from the Master's Lodgings, on the Ides of October, 1612. ❧  CHAPTER THE FIRST Of my Lineage and Birth; of the Prodigies that attended it; and of my first Emendations, which were ill received בְּרֵאשִׁית, saith Moses: In the Beginning. Since that great Author hath begun at the beginning, and I can find no fault with his method (though I have found several with his Vowel-points), I shall do likewise. Our House is of great Antiquity. The vulgar derive the name of Hulse from some Cheshire hamlet or other. I derive it, with better reason, from Hylas, the beloved squire of Hercules, who sailed in the Argo. Ὕλας, by the loss of an aspirate (which the English have ever been careless of) and the stiffening of the final sibilant, becomes Hulse, as any man may see who hath eyes and is not a Fellow of this College. That Hylas was drawn down into a well by Nymphs, and is not recorded to have left issue, I account no objection. Apollonius is silent upon the point, and silence in an Author is consent in a Critick. Let Scaliger boast of his Princes of Verona; I have the Argonauts. I was born at Sheffield in Hallamshire, among the Cutlers, from whom I have my Edge. My Mother, being near her time, dreamt she was delivered not of a son but of a Pen-knife. The Cunning Woman of Ecclesall interpreted this to signify a Surgeon, and my Father a Cutler. Both were wrong: it signified a Critick, whose office is to cut. There was a second Prodigy. As bees settled upon the lips of the infant Pindar and made honey there, so a swarm of wasps settled upon mine, and made none. My enemies have since turned this into a verse: Hulsius e cunis vespas, non mella, ferebat. That is: Hulse, from his very cradle, bore wasps and not honey. I gloss it thus: Hulsius. Correctly Latinised, which is more than its authors can manage in their own Disputations. e cunis. True. I have never been idle. vespas, non mella. A false antithesis. The wasp is the nobler creature: it does not labour for the benefit of a Bee-keeper, as a Fellow labours for a Bursar. ferebat. Read ferebat with gloria, understood. I have so emended it in my own copy. My first word, as my Nurse deposed upon oath, was neither Mother nor Father but Sic?. I uttered it with a rising inflexion, upon hearing my Father say grace before meat. At seven years I was sent to the Grammar School, under Mr. Ezekiel Thwaite, a man of large hand and small learning. On the first morning we were set to construe Lily's verses, Propria quae maribus tribuuntur mascula dicas. I observed aloud that the line was flat, the doctrine doubtful, and the Author dead and in no condition to object, and I offered a better reading. I was flogged. I took the flogging to be Mr. Thwaite's Apparatus Criticus, and it was the fullest he ever compiled. Within the year we came to Virgil, Arma virumque cano. I pointed out that Virgil, being a modest and retiring man, would never say of himself I sing. The true reading is plainly Arma virumque CAVE: Beware of arms, and of the man. This is both a sounder Doctrine and better advice. I was flogged again. Here I first learned the Law, since verified upon every Fellow of this College, that the reception of a Conjecture is in inverse proportion to its Brilliance. Homer fared no better at my hands, nor I at Mr. Thwaite's. Ἄνδρα μοι ἔννεπε, Μοῦσα, πολύτροπον, Tell me, Muse, of the man of many turns. But I had walked to Hull and observed the Sailors there, who have many turns indeed, and all of them towards the Alehouse. I therefore restored πολύποτον, the man of many draughts. This reading I yet maintain. When I wrote of it to Mr. Casaubon, he did not answer, which I take to be assent. Of that same Casaubon, and of Scaliger, and of the great Quarrel of the Digamma, I shall speak in their place. Here I record only the sentence I composed in Greek upon leaving school, which I have since had carved above my study door: τίς γὰρ ἂν ἐμοῦ κριτικώτερος γένοιτο; οὐδεὶς δήπου, οὐδ᾽ αὐτὸς ὁ Σκαλίγερος ὁ ψευδοβασιλεύς. That is: For who could be more critical than I? No one, surely; not even Scaliger himself, the pretended King. The Fellows have taken to reading the first clause aloud as they pass, and omitting the rest. Their eventual descent of the great Staircase was occasioned in part by this; but that belongs to Chapter the Ninth. Given at the Master's Lodgings, St. Polyrots, upon the Feast of St. Jerome, Patron of all who correct the Texts of others and quarrel with their friends, Anno 1612. N.B. The Printer informs me that he hath corrected certain Errors in the foregoing. I shall attend to him upon the Stairs. ❧ CHAPTER THE SECOND Of my going up to the University; of the Disputation upon Homer; of the Great Snow Controversy; and how I came to be elected Fellow of St. Polyrots, against the Wishes of all Men but One I went up to the University in my sixteenth year, with a box of books, a suit of black, and a letter from Mr. Thwaite. I am told it described me as ingenio acri, moribus acrioribus: of sharp wit and sharper manners. On the first morning I wrote my name in the Matriculation Book and corrected the Registrar's Latin in the line above. It was an inauspicious beginning, and the Registrar never forgave me. He was, however, wrong about the ablative. My Tutor was Dr. Mordecai Grubbe, a learned man in the Hebrew, from whom I learned that tongue for one sufficient reason: that I might have more Authors to correct. Dr. Grubbe held that the Vowel-points were given to Moses on Sinai. I held that they were added by some Rabbi of Tiberias with a weak eye and a strong thirst. We disputed it for three years, at the end of which he was dead. I do not say the two things were connected, but I do not say they were not. In my second year I was put up to dispute in the Schools upon the Question, An Homerus fuerit ebrius?: Whether Homer were drunk. I took the Affirmative and argued it from πολύποτον, which the Reader will remember. The Respondent was one Mr. Lancelot Gudgeon of Emmanuel, a pale young man who ate no meat on Fridays and very little on the other days. He denied my major premise, my minor premise, and finally my conclusion. At this I put him out of the window. We were on the ground floor, so he took no harm but to his gown, and the Moderator declared the Disputation drawn. It was the beginning of a Friendship of the kind that Scholars enjoy: that is, a lifelong Enmity, conducted in print. The occasion of our open War was a single word of Horace: Vides ut alta stet nive candidum Soracte... You see how Soracte stands white with deep snow... I observed that within six lines the Poet calls for wine, deprome quadrimum Sabina... merum diota, "draw off the four-year-old neat wine from its Sabine jar." I observed further that a mountain does not stand in snow, but a man may very well stand in wine, if he hath drunk enough of it. I therefore restored vino for nive: Soracte, white with Falernian. The Falernian is white, whatever the Ignorant suppose, and I had a cask of it to prove it. Mr. Gudgeon replied within the month with a pamphlet, Nix Vindicata, or the Snow Restored, in which he styled me Hulsius Vinosus. I answered with Antinix, or the Snowball Returned, which opens thus: ὦ χιονόφρων Γουδγεών, ψυχρότερος εἶ τῆς σῆς χιόνος. I gloss it, for the benefit of the Fellows: ὦ χιονόφρων. O snow-minded. My own coinage, and better than any of his. Γουδγεών. His name, ennobled by the Greek, which it hath not deserved. ψυχρότερος εἶ. You are colder. But mark the double edge. ψυχρός is also the word by which Aristotle and Longinus condemn a frigid style, tasteless and overwrought. So I say at once that he is cold, and that he writes badly. Two wounds with one stroke: this is the Hulsian manner. τῆς σῆς χιόνος. Than your own snow. For it is his snow now, Horace having disowned it. He replied with Hulsiomastix. I replied with Gudgeonomachia, in four books, with an Index of his Errors longer than the work itself. The Stationers grew rich upon us both. Now it fell out that in that same year a Fellowship lay vacant at St. Polyrots. The name of that College, I may here remark, is not derived, as the Fellows foolishly maintain, from some Saint unknown to the Calendar. It comes from the Greek πολυρρόθιος, much-roaring, said of the sea. It is my own conjecture, and so apt that if Homer did not use the word, he ought to have. Mr. Gudgeon and I stood for the place together. The Fellows divided equally, being equally afraid of us both, and the Election fell to the old Master, Dr. Ambrose Fothergill, who was deaf, ninety, and fond of his dinner. Mr. Gudgeon spoke first, in tolerable Latin, for an hour. Upon the word vērēcundia he gave the second syllable short. I coughed. It was a small cough, but well placed, and Dr. Fothergill, who could not hear the Last Trump, heard that. I spoke next, for three hours and a quarter, upon the Excellence of Myself. Long before the end the Master's dinner was cold, the Fellows were asleep, and Mr. Gudgeon had gone home. I was declared elected nemine contradicente, there being, by that hour, no one left to contradict. That evening I wrote in the College Bible, beside the 118th Psalm: אֶבֶן מָאֲסוּ הַבּוֹנִים הָיְתָה לְרֹאשׁ פִּנָּה The stone which the builders refused is become the head of the corner. The builders I took to be the Fellows. They took the stone to be what I should presently be thrown with, and in this, as in all things, they were mistaken. Mr. Gudgeon is now, by the malice of the Statutes, my Vice-Master. He sits opposite me at High Table, where I observe that he takes his Snow with a great deal of Falernian. Given at the Master's Lodgings, upon the Feast of St. Francis, who preached to the Birds, being unable to get a hearing from the Fellows, Anno 1612. [In the margin, in another hand: Nix. — L.G.] ❧ ✠ ❧ ✠ FINIS PARTIS PRIMAE ✠ ❧ ✠

🤖🚨 OPENAI DISRUPTS 15,000-USER CAMPAIGN TRYING TO EXTRACT HIDDEN AI REASONING  OpenAI has disclosed a large-scale operation designed to extract the protected reasoning of its AI models.  The activity is consistent with:  ADVERSARIAL DISTILLATION  OpenAI identified related activity across a cluster of more than:  15,000 USERS.  A core cluster was attributed by OpenAI to individuals associated with:  MOONSHOT AI  the Chinese AI company behind Kimi.  The operation began July 1.  Then activity surged.  On July 24–25 alone, OpenAI detected:  * 16,000 extraction-pattern requests * More than 4,000 users involved  One technique was particularly interesting.  Operators copied ENCRYPTED REASONING from one conversation and attempted to get a model in another conversation to:  DECRYPT + TRANSCRIBE IT.  Independent researchers also discovered related cross-model and conversation-compaction vulnerabilities.  OpenAI investigated those findings and confirmed the attack paths were REAL.  The company has now closed a pathway where someone who already possessed another user's encrypted reasoning could replay it and recover its contents.  Important distinction:  * OpenAI says attackers did NOT break its encryption * They did NOT compromise an OpenAI database * They did NOT gain direct access to stored user conversations  Instead, they manipulated model interactions to reproduce protected reasoning in requester-visible forms.  OpenAI says the broader campaign was fully disrupted by July 28.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  Model theft is evolving beyond stealing weights or API outputs.  Protected reasoning itself is becoming a HIGH-VALUE TARGET.  At scale, extracting reasoning can help another model reproduce capabilities without paying the same training, research and safety costs.  There is also a security consequence:  A distilled model could inherit advanced capabilities WITHOUT inheriting the original model's safeguards.  OpenAI explicitly warns that this becomes increasingly relevant as frontier models gain capabilities in dual-use domains.  This may become the AI equivalent of intellectual-property theft combined with capability proliferation.  openai.com/index/disrupting-… #OpenAI #MoonshotAI #Kimi #AISecurity #AI #ModelSecurity #ThreatIntel #DDW

🇨🇳🚨 CHINA-NEXUS WARLOCK RANSOMWARE HITS WATER + TELECOM INFRASTRUCTURE  New Symantec research reveals continued activity from the China-nexus threat actor tracked as:  LONGLEGS / STORM-2603  Over the past two months, the group attacked at least four organizations:  * Water utility * Telecommunications provider * Regional government organization * University  Victims were located across Europe, Africa and Latin America, particularly in Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries.  Initial access continues to involve vulnerabilities in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint.  But what happened AFTER compromise is particularly interesting.  In one critical-infrastructure intrusion, attackers pushed an AV/EDR-killing tool to more than:  40 HOSTS IN ABOUT TWO HOURS.  They abused K7RKScan — a legitimately signed but vulnerable driver affected by CVE-2025-1055 — to terminate protected security processes at KERNEL LEVEL.  Then Warlock was deployed to at least:  33 SYSTEMS.  Instead of relying entirely on conventional remote-deployment tooling, the attackers placed the ransomware inside the domain's:  SYSVOL SHARE.  Active Directory's normal replication infrastructure then helped distribute the payload across the environment.  Longlegs also abused Visual Studio Code's built-in tunneling capability, installing:  code-insiders.exe  as a service to establish covert remote access that could resemble legitimate developer/admin traffic.  The intrusion chain included:  * SharePoint exploitation * ASPX webshell deployment * ASP.NET machine-key theft * Forged signed payloads * DLL sideloading * Legitimate cloud-storage services for payload delivery * BYOVD security-tool termination * VS Code tunneling * SYSVOL-based ransomware deployment  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is a useful reminder that ransomware operators don't always need exotic lateral-movement malware.  Once Active Directory is compromised, the infrastructure administrators rely on to distribute legitimate enterprise content can become the attacker's deployment mechanism.  In this case:  THE DOMAIN HELPED DISTRIBUTE THE RANSOMWARE.  security.com/threat-intellig… #Warlock #Storm2603 #Longlegs #Ransomware #SharePoint #ActiveDirectory #ThreatIntel #DDW

sample_tweets.text: Only a tiny fraction of the world’s mosquito species prey on humans. All of these are invasive across essentially their entire range, having tagged along with humans as we moved around the world. Multiple careful studies say that eliminating these species would have little or no impact on the environment. However, it would save at least a million human lives a year, and get rid of a constant source of discomfort that prevents people from safely spending as much time outside as they would prefer. Malaria is only one of dozens of diseases, many potentially fatal, spread by mosquitoes. Gene drives can safely and relatively inexpensively eliminate these parasitic insects; we can create male mosquitoes that can only have male offspring and which then crash the population. It’s well past time that we did it.

New: iPhones have an automatic reboot feature which quietly reboots the phone after a certain time; cops were freaking out about this when we revealed it in 2024. Now, phone hackers have a way around it, according to a leaked video  404media.co/cops-can-bypass-…

Let me tell you how I delayed WinXP SP2 for a month.  My software (BlackICE) was on the list of software that had to work. When they made major changes to the kernel network stack, my software broke.  They grabbed their reverse engineers to figure out why. What they discovered was that my software doing something evil, patching the kernel's network stack when our software was loaded. That's tricky on a multi-CPU system with warring instruction/data caches. We wrote a patent on how to do it reliably without crashing the system.  We searched through the kernel to find the location we needed to patch, looking for a certain pattern of bytes. They changed the network stack so that thing we were patching no longer existed.  So to make our software work, the inserted that pattern back into the kernel. As packets arrived, the new function would jump to that pattern, and then after, jump right back. This way, we could find the pattern and patch it -- and thereby patch the intended function.  Some Microsoft lawyers wanted to sue us for violating the software license agreement, which forbids reverse engineering, which we had to do in order to patch the kernel at runtime.  Cooler heads prevailed.  The point is our software did an ugly hack in order to work, and then Microsoft did an even crazier, uglier hack so that we'd keep working.  For years after, when meeting Microsoft engineers at conferences, they'd love to yell at me.  When Vista came along, they added signing of kernel models, putting an end to such nonsense, but also providing a real documented API we could use.

🟡 위협 점수: 5/10 (보통)

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 공격은 AI 에이전트를 활용하여 취약점 스캔부터 공격 실행까지의 타임라인을 극단적으로 단축하는 'Autonomous Cyberattack' 형태로 진화하고 있습니다. 특히 공격자들은 EDR 탐지를 우회하기 위해 BYOVD(Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) 기법을 사용하거나, 브라우저 기반 공격을 통해 엔드포인트 아티팩트를 남기지 않는 은밀한 방식을 선호하고 있습니다 ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-edr-blind-spot-3-ways-browser-attacks-evade-endpoint-telemetry/)). 또한, 소프트웨어 공급망 공격이 단순 타이포스쿼팅을 넘어 다단계 C2 체인을 갖춘 정교한 형태로 발전하고 있어 기업의 오픈소스 패키지 관리에 비상이 걸렸습니다 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5782)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **KillSec**: 16세 소년이 주도한 것으로 알려진 랜섬웨어 그룹으로, 2년간 약 500개 조직을 공격한 후 인프라가 압수되고 핵심 멤버 3명이 체포됨 ([CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/killsec-ransomware-group-arrests-operation-killswitch/)).
- **TA419**: AI 정책 전문가 및 미국 싱크탱크를 타겟으로 한 피싱 캠페인을 수행하며 클라우드 계정 탈취를 시도함 ([CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/china-cyber-espionage-ta419-phishing-us-ai-policy-experts/)).
- **ShinyHunters**: 데이터 탈취 및 갈취 혐의로 네덜란드 경찰이 23세 핵심 인물을 체포함 ([Krebs on Security](https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/09/dutch-police-arrest-reformed-hacker-in-shiny-hunters-investigation/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **신한은행 및 국내 기업**: AI 자율 침투 도구를 이용한 공격으로 신한은행 고객 정보 유출 및 무신사, 강남언니 등 국내 기업 대상 API 권한 검증 허점을 노린 공격 발생 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208718)).
- **카카오톡 사칭 악성코드**: SEO Poisoning을 통해 카카오톡 설치 파일로 위장한 악성코드가 국내 유포 중 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95641/)).
- **리눅스 임플란트**: BPFDoor, Rekoobe, AVERAT 등이 한국 및 대만의 통신/메일 게이트웨이 장비를 타겟으로 활동 중 ([DFIR_Radar](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2106022326546657725)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-76460**: Cisco ISE, CVSS 10.0, 인증되지 않은 원격 코드 실행, 즉시 패치 권고 ([johnmcclure00](https://twitter.com/johnmcclure00/status/2106023654303711443)).
- **CVE-2026-76504**: Cisco SD-WAN Manager, CVSS 9.8, 인증 우회, KEV 등재 ([uwillc](https://twitter.com/uwillc/status/2106021921477300267)).
- **CVE-2026-19445**: Python CPython, CVSS 9.2, Use-after-free 취약점 ([ridvanyagli](https://twitter.com/ridvanyagli/status/2105823850474725746)).
- **CVE-2026-88771/88772**: Citrix NetScaler, 심각도 높음, 야생에서 악용 중 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)).
- **CVE-2026-104286**: FortiMail, 경로 탐색(Path Traversal) 제로데이, 악용 중 ([DFIR_Radar](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2105992045915685098)).

### 5. IOC 요약
